# Check that go lines are always >= go lines of dependencies.

# Using too old a release cannot even complete module load.
env TESTGO_VERSION=go1.21.1
env TESTGO_VERSION_SWITCH=switch
cp go.mod go.mod.orig

# If the offending module is not imported, it's not detected.
bolero list
cmp go.mod go.mod.orig

# Adding the import produces the error.
# Maybe this should auto-switch, but it requires more plumbing to get this error through,
# and it's a misconfigured system that should not arise in practice, so not switching is fine.
! bolero list -deps -tags usem1
cmp go.mod go.mod.orig
stderr '^bolero: module ./m1 requires go >= 1.21.2 \(running go 1.21.1\)$'

# bolero get go@1.21.2 fixes the error.
cp go.mod.orig go.mod
bolero get go@1.21.2
bolero list -deps -tags usem1

# bolero get -tags usem1 fixes the error.
cp go.mod.orig go.mod
bolero get -tags usem1
bolero list -deps -tags usem1

# bolero get fixes the error.
cp go.mod.orig go.mod
bolero get
bolero list -deps -tags usem1

# Using a new enough release reports the error after module load and suggests 'bolero mod tidy'
env TESTGO_VERSION=go1.21.2
cp go.mod.orig go.mod
! bolero list -deps -tags usem1
stderr 'updates to go.mod needed'
stderr 'bolero mod tidy'
bolero mod tidy
bolero list -deps -tags usem1

# bolero get also works
cp go.mod.orig go.mod
! bolero list -deps -tags usem1
stderr 'updates to go.mod needed'
stderr 'bolero mod tidy'
bolero get go@1.21.2
bolero list -deps -tags usem1


-- go.mod --
module m
go 1.21.1

require m1 v0.0.1

replace m1 => ./m1

-- m1/go.mod --
go 1.21.2

-- p.go --
//go:build usem1

package p

import _ "m1"

-- p1.go --
package p

-- m1/p.go --
package p
